title: Cost attribution data audit (Usage Insights) — telemetry fields, gaps, and validation plan
content:
Doc purpose
This is a working audit of our current telemetry/metering signals as they relate to in-console “Usage Insights” (cost + usage breakdown by API route and model), with a focus on:
- What fields we have today (and where they live)
- Known gaps that block accurate route/model attribution and “top cost driver” explanations
- Proposed instrumentation + schema changes
- A validation plan to prove we match billing totals and behave well under cardinality and late events

Owners / reviewers
- Primary: Caleb Johnson (Observability) + Nadia Rahman (Cost attribution pipeline)
- Partners: Logan Wright (Telemetry & Analytics), Thomas Baird (Telemetry perf/cardinality), Chloe Martin (Console backend), Dylan Brooks (Console), Allison Grant (Observability quality)

Scope and context
Usage Insights needs consistent, aggregatable dimensions:
- workspace_id / project_id (and env, if applicable)
- time bucket (hour/day)
- route (canonical/normalized)
- model (stable family + version + provider alias mapping)
Optional dimensions: deployment_mode, region, cache hit/miss, retries, fallbacks, streaming

We must support:
- Route+model tables that sum to the same totals as Billing for a given filter set/time range
- “Top cost drivers” / “What changed?” heuristics requiring deltas in tokens, cache hit rate, retry rate, fallbacks, and context length distribution


Data sources audited (current state)
1) gateway_request_events (HTTP/gRPC gateway)
- Purpose: request-level telemetry at the edge, good for route/endpoint and request metadata
- Typical availability: near-real-time, but not authoritative for final cost (tokens/caching may be downstream)

2) inference_metering_events (metering pipeline)
- Purpose: authoritative token counts and cost inputs, used for billing hooks
- Typical availability: may lag; may emit multiple events per user request (retries/fallbacks/chunks)

3) runtime_generation_events (serving runtime)
- Purpose: performance/caching signals (KV cache, batching) + tokenization details
- Typical availability: high volume; not always joined cleanly to billing/metering

4) billing_line_item_hooks (billing)
- Purpose: final charge computation and invoicing
- Note: this is our ground truth for “totals,” but it is not dimensioned enough for route breakdown without upstream tags


Field inventory (what we have today)
Below is an inventory of fields we currently see with reasonable consistency (>=95% populated unless noted). Names are normalized here for readability; actual internal field names vary by service.

A) Common identifiers
- request_id: present in gateway; present in metering most of the time; sometimes rotated on retries
- trace_id/span_id: present for some SDKs; inconsistent for older clients
- workspace_id: present in metering; sometimes missing in gateway for legacy API key auth flow (see gaps)
- project_id: present for most hosted API traffic; Dedicated/Private traffic varies depending on control plane integration
- api_key_id: present (sensitive); should not be exposed in Insights but useful for debugging joins

B) Dimensions needed for breakdowns
- model: present in metering; sometimes alias (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b”) vs full pinned version
- region: present in gateway and metering; region naming differs (e.g., “us-east-1” vs “use1”)
- deployment_mode: present in control plane metadata; not always propagated into metering events
- route / endpoint:
  - gateway path: raw_path generally present, but not normalized
  - route name: present for some internal services, missing for OpenAI-compat endpoints and some streaming variants

C) Usage and cost driver fields
- prompt_tokens (tokens_in): present in metering (authoritative)
- completion_tokens (tokens_out): present in metering (authoritative)
- total_tokens: derived
- cached_prompt_tokens: partial availability; depends on runtime + metering integration
- cache_hit: inconsistent definition across runtime vs metering (boolean vs percentage; see gaps)
- context_length: derivable (prompt_tokens), but distribution requires sampling or bucketing
- latency_ms:
  - gateway: request_latency_ms (end-to-end)
  - runtime: time_to_first_token_ms, tokens_per_second, queue_ms (partial)
- streaming:
  - is_streaming: present in gateway for SSE/websocket; missing in some metering records
  - stream_chunks: runtime only; not joined consistently
- retries:
  - retry_count: present in gateway (client-visible retries) but not always aligned with metering’s notion of “attempts”
  - attempt_id: runtime sometimes emits; metering does not consistently carry
- fallbacks:
  - fallback_model: present in runtime logs; metering sometimes only reports final model billed


Gaps / issues (blockers and quality concerns)
1) Route attribution is not reliable across all endpoints
- OpenAI-compat endpoints: we often only capture raw_path (e.g., “/v1/chat/completions”) but the gateway does not always emit a stable “route” dimension usable as a key.
- Dynamic paths: internal/private endpoints can include IDs in the path (e.g., “/v1/projects/123/…”) causing cardinality explosion if we group on raw_path.
- Streaming variants: in at least one region we have missing route tags for streaming endpoints (reported in Slack: eng-platform/1738527701). When route is missing, console tables either drop rows or show “unknown,” which breaks customer trust.

2) Model identity is not stable enough for reporting
- Model aliases: same underlying pinned model can appear under different aliases; exports can show duplicates (related to support ticket SUP-24844).
- Version bucketing: we need a stable “model_family” + “model_version” that won’t change when marketing names or aliases shift.

3) Retry + fallback semantics are inconsistent
- “What counts as a retry?” differs by layer:
  - gateway may retry upstream on transient 5xx
  - runtime may do an internal re-attempt
  - metering may emit multiple partial events (attempts) but not label them clearly
- For fallbacks, metering frequently only reflects final billed model, which hides the cause (“fallback from X to Y due to capacity”). This limits the explainability for “top drivers” and hides reliability/cost tradeoffs.

4) Cache metrics are not in a single authoritative place
- runtime: knows KV cache hits, prefix cache, batching effectiveness
- metering: knows billed tokens vs cached tokens only if we explicitly pass that detail along
- Today, cached_prompt_tokens is frequently null and cache_hit is not consistently defined.

5) Joining events across systems is brittle
- request_id isn’t always stable across retries/fallbacks (sometimes new request_id for attempt)
- trace_id coverage is incomplete
- This makes it hard to attribute tokens/cost to the original route and to produce accurate driver explanations.

6) Late events and data freshness
- Metering events can arrive late relative to the gateway timestamp, especially for long generations and backpressure.
- For console correctness: late arrival is fine if our aggregation handles it, but we need explicit lag measurement + user-facing freshness metadata.

7) Missing/partial workspace/project IDs in some flows
- Legacy API key auth path: gateway logs may lack workspace_id (observed in a small but non-trivial subset).
- Private deployments: project/workspace mapping depends on control plane integration; some customers have “workspace only” mapping.


Proposed changes (instrumentation + schema)
A) Standardize route dimensions with explicit normalized_route
Goal: make route a first-class, low-cardinality dimension emitted at ingestion (not reconstructed later).
- Add fields (gateway → metering):
  - raw_path (string): exact incoming HTTP path
  - normalized_route (string): templated path with params removed (e.g., “/v1/projects/:project_id/chat/completions”)
  - route_source (string): “gateway”, “sdk”, or “unknown”
- Implement route normalization library shared by gateway + telemetry (ENG-3813). Rules must live in an ADR and be versioned.
- For OpenAI-compat endpoints, normalized_route should map to the canonical documented route (e.g., “/v1/chat/completions”).

B) Stabilize model reporting keys
Goal: avoid duplicates and support rollups by “family” and “pinned version.”
- Add fields (control plane/model registry → metering):
  - model_family (string): e.g., “llama-3.1-70b”
  - model_version (string): stable pinned version or digest-like identifier
  - model_alias (string): user-facing alias used in request (optional)
  - model_provider (string): “redwood”, “openai-compat”, etc.
- Track mapping changes in a single source of truth; don’t infer in the warehouse. See ENG-3823.

C) Clarify retries and attempts
Goal: make “retries” a dimension we can explain without double-counting.
- Add fields:
  - request_group_id (string): stable id for the logical user request (shared across attempts)
  - attempt_id (string/int): monotonically increasing attempt counter within request_group_id
  - attempt_reason (string): “retry_transient”, “fallback_capacity”, “fallback_policy”, “client_cancelled”, etc.
- Metering should emit per-attempt tokens and costs (so we can attribute extra spend to retries/fallbacks explicitly).

D) Cache attribution fields
Goal: enable “cache hit/miss” driver and verify token economics.
- Add fields:
  - billed_prompt_tokens (int)
  - cached_prompt_tokens (int)
  - cache_strategy (string): “kv_prefix”, “full_prefix”, “none”, “unknown”
  - cache_hit (boolean): defined as cached_prompt_tokens > 0 (simple) OR more nuanced % bucket; pick one definition and document it
- Preference: store both raw counts + derived % in queries, to avoid ambiguity.

E) Deployment + region normalization
Goal: ensure consistent filtering and rollups.
- Add normalized_region (string) with a controlled vocabulary
- Ensure deployment_mode is set for all events: “hosted”, “dedicated”, “private_vpc”, “on_prem”

F) Versioning and compatibility
- Add telemetry_schema_version to metering events so aggregations can handle migrations safely.
- Maintain backward-compat in query service by deriving missing normalized_route/model_family for older records where possible, but tag as “derived” so we can audit quality.


Validation plan (prove correctness + catch regressions)
1) Billing reconciliation (must-have)
- Daily automated job compares:
  - Sum(cost_usd) in insights aggregates vs billing_line_item_hooks totals
  - By workspace_id + day (and optionally by project_id)
- Tolerance policy:
  - 0.1–0.5% acceptable drift depending on rounding and timing windows
  - >0.5% triggers investigation; >1% pages on-call for insights pipeline during beta
- Include “explain drift” logging: late events count, missing-route share, missing-model share.

2) Route coverage and unknown bucket monitoring
- Track % of metering cost that has normalized_route populated.
- Alert if:
  - unknown route cost share > 0.5% for hosted OR changes by >0.2% day-over-day
  - any single region has unknown route > 1% (streaming region issue class)

3) Model mapping sanity checks
- Report duplicate rows risk:
  - detect multiple model_version values mapping to same alias in same day without an explicit rollout
  - detect same model_version appearing under multiple model_family values (should not happen)

4) Retry/fallback accounting checks
- Ensure request_group_id rollups:
  - total attempts >= 1
  - cost attributed to retries equals sum of attempts beyond attempt_id=1
- Verify that “fallback” attempts are labeled and model transitions are captured.

5) Sampling + trace-based joins for ground truth
- For a small sample (e.g., 1k requests/day), log an “audit bundle” record that includes:
  - gateway request metadata (raw_path, normalized_route, is_streaming)
  - runtime caching + fallback details
  - metering token/cost outputs
- Use this for debugging and to validate that our joins don’t misattribute.

6) Performance / cardinality guardrails
- Ensure normalized_route doesn’t explode:
  - target: < 200 unique normalized_route per workspace/day for typical customers
  - cap: enforce a maximum unique routes per workspace/day in aggregation job (spill to “other/overflow” with a warning)
- Add a weekly report of top route cardinality offenders to feed normalization improvements.


Implementation notes / next steps (near-term)
- Route normalization library (ENG-3813): prioritize OpenAI-compat and streaming variants; include test fixtures for dynamic paths.
- Metering changes to accept normalized_route + request_group_id (ENG-3822 + follow-up): coordinate with Nadia + Logan.
- Model bucketing fields (ENG-3823): align with model registry team; decide canonical “version” format.
- Reconciliation job (ENG-3817): implement daily diff; wire alerts (beta thresholds TBD).
- Data freshness metrics: compute “max_event_time” and “ingestion_lag_p95” per workspace; surface in console as “data current as of …” (ENG-3824).


Open questions
1) What is the definitive definition of “route”? (Docs + UX)
- Do we want route to reflect external API paths only, or include internal/private endpoints?
- Suggestion: show “API route” as the canonical external path, and hide internal-only routes unless explicitly enabled.

2) Should we attribute cost to original requested model or billed model?
- For fallbacks, finance cares about billed model; engineers care about “requested vs actual.”
- Proposal: store both requested_model_* and billed_model_*; default UI uses billed, with a toggle in drill-down.

3) Streaming overhead
- Do we need a first-class metric for “streaming overhead cost” (extra retries/chunks) or just expose latency + retry deltas?

4) Backfill expectations
- If we add normalized_route/model_family fields now, what’s the plan for historical data?
- Proposal: no hard backfill for beta; provide a “data starts on <date>” note and backfill best-effort for top workspaces if needed.

Appendix A — Proposed minimum metering event shape (for discussion)
(Note: illustrative only; exact schema lives with telemetry platform. Listing here to make gaps concrete.)
- event_time
- ingestion_time
- workspace_id
- project_id
- request_group_id
- attempt_id
- request_id
- normalized_route
- raw_path (optional / debug)
- is_streaming
- deployment_mode
- normalized_region
- model_family
- model_version
- model_alias (optional)
- prompt_tokens
- completion_tokens
- billed_prompt_tokens
- cached_prompt_tokens
- retry_reason / attempt_reason
- fallback_from_model_family (optional)
- latency_ms (optional)
- cost_usd (computed field or compute inputs)

Appendix B — Known incidents / customer-facing issues tied to gaps
- Missing route breakdown for OpenAI-compat endpoints: support ticket SUP-24827 (route mapping)
- Export CSV duplicate rows due to model aliases: SUP-24844 (model bucketing)
- Totals mismatch vs invoice: SUP-24811 (reconciliation + rounding + timing windows)

Change log
- 2026-01-10: Initial audit draft (Caleb)
- 2026-01-22: Added model alias/version notes after export spec review + support feedback (Caleb)
- 2026-02-05: Added streaming region gap + request_group_id proposal after eng-platform thread (Caleb)
